units.text: INT. DINNER THEATER - BACKSTAGE - NIGHT
A cramped corridor behind a painted flat.
Costume racks, a mirror ringed with bulbs, a prop table covered in plastic daggers and one real turkey leg.
Muffled laughter from the audience.
BARNABY CROWE (50s, leading man, powdered wig, gout slipper) strides in and flings his hat on the table.
Behind him, DIANTHA FOSTER (30s, ingénue, corset half-laced) hurries, hem in her fist.
Last in is STAGE MANAGER GWENDOLYN "GWEN" TAKAHASHI (40s, black clothes, headset, clipboard) who reads from her list as she walks.
Who moved my snuffbox?
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: It's on the mantle, Mr. Crowe.
units.name: GWEN

units.text: There is no mantle!
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: It's painted.
units.name: GWEN

units.text: I will not play Hamlet opposite a painted mantle.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Barnaby, it's "Much Ado."
units.name: DIANTHA

units.text: Is it? I thought we'd done that.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Five minutes, people.
units.name: GWEN

units.text: Breathe. Breathe. It's only two hundred people and a soup course.
units.name: DIANTHA

units.text: Darling, you were magnificent in act one.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: I forgot my line.
units.name: DIANTHA

units.text: Nobody noticed.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: You said "well-played" and then walked offstage.
units.name: DIANTHA

units.text: It was a very good pause.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Diantha, your cue is the bell. Mr. Crowe, yours is when she starts to cry.
units.name: GWEN

units.text: She's crying?
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Not yet.
units.name: DIANTHA

units.text: Then enter on the bell.
units.name: GWEN

units.text: A bell tolls, loud, from the stage.
All three freeze, then bolt through the curtain in a flurry of lace and a clatter of turkey bones.
